cards.name: 3-Point Ellipse
cards.summary: Draws an ellipse from its axis: you first drag a line that sets the ellipse's centre line (length and angle), then move the pointer away from that line to set the height and click. The result is an ordinary ellipse object, already tilted to whatever angle the first line had.
cards.how: Pick it from the Ellipse Tools flyout (Toolbox). Press and drag to draw the centre line through the ellipse (this fixes one axis and its angle), release, move the pointer away from the line to set the height, and click to finish. The property bar offers Ellipse / Pie / Arc and start / end angles, same as the Ellipse tool.
cards.script_api: Select the tool: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem "0b4cd8b0-f5bf-47c4-9072-f17bc053d2ef" (cdr_guid; no Application.ActiveTool value exists for it, the harvest read back -1). Produce the same result without the tool: ActiveLayer.CreateEllipse2(CenterX, CenterY, Radius1, Radius2) then Shape.Rotate(Angle) (or set Shape.RotationAngle).
use_for: tilted ellipse for an orbit ring or planet ring
ellipse lying along a diagonal guide in a layout
ellipse whose width must match an existing slanted edge
angled lens flare or highlight shape
avoid: axis-aligned ellipses and circles: the Ellipse tool (F7) is faster
exact sizes and angles: draw with the Ellipse tool and type width, height and rotation in the property bar
perspective-correct circles on a surface: draw a circle and use Object > Perspective > Add Perspective or the Envelope instead

review.changes: summary: "other half-axis" replaced by "height" (the click sets the height, as how says); how: removed the unverified Ctrl angle-step modifier; avoid: Add Perspective menu path corrected to Object > Perspective > Add Perspective (the v25 path in the harvest, not Effects).

cards.name: Ellipse
cards.summary: Draws an ellipse or circle by dragging its bounding box; the result is a native ellipse object that stays editable as an ellipse, pie or arc (start and end angles) until it is converted to curves.
cards.how: Press F7 (or pick Ellipse in the Ellipse Tools flyout) and drag diagonally on the page. Ctrl while dragging makes a perfect circle, Shift draws from the centre outward, Ctrl+Shift a circle from the centre. The property bar switches Ellipse / Pie / Arc, sets start and end angles and direction, and takes exact width, height and position.
cards.script_api: Select the tool: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem "1810af9f-140f-4b22-945a-7087ba60ee91" or Application.ActiveTool = 4 (cdrToolDrawEllipse). Draw the shape directly: ActiveLayer.CreateEllipse(Left, Top, Right, Bottom, StartAngle, EndAngle, Pie), ActiveLayer.CreateEllipse2(CenterX, CenterY, Radius1, Radius2) or ActiveLayer.CreateEllipseRect(Rect).
use_for: circular badge or seal base
dots and bullets in an infographic
logo circle and ring construction
pie or arc segments for a simple chart
ellipse placeholder for a portrait crop via PowerClip
avoid: ellipse at an angle along a guide: use 3-Point Ellipse
shapes you will node-edit freely: convert to curves first (Ctrl+Q), after which the arc / pie controls are gone
concentric rings: draw one circle and use Contour instead of drawing each by hand

review.changes: how: removed "double-clicking the tool button draws a page-sized ellipse", which is the Rectangle tool's page-frame behaviour copied onto this tool. Ctrl+Q in avoid checked against the harvest (Object/Convert to Curves).

cards.name: Attributes Eyedropper
cards.summary: Copies object attributes from one object to others: you sample a source object, then click target objects to give them its fill, outline and text properties and, if enabled, its transformations (size, rotation, position) and effects such as contour, drop shadow, envelope or perspective. Nothing visible changes until a target is clicked.
cards.how: Pick it from the Eyedropper flyout. In the property bar open the Properties, Transformations and Effects lists and tick only what should be copied. Click the source object to sample; the cursor turns into a paint bucket, then click each target object to apply.
cards.script_api: Select the tool: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem "87bf2821-a06a-42ff-b5ca-bc7ae2d64e10" (no Application.ActiveTool value; the harvest read back -1). Copy the same properties by script: Shape.CopyPropertiesFrom(Source, cdrCopyFill + cdrCopyOutlinePen + cdrCopyOutlineColor + cdrCopyTextAttrs), or Fill.CopyAssign / Outline.CopyAssign; transformations through SetSize / RotationAngle / SetPosition and effects by recreating them (e.g. Shape.CreateDropShadow, Shape.CreateContour) - there is no single call that copies effects.
use_for: make every caption box match a styled master box
copy a drop shadow or contour from one icon to a set of icons
copy text formatting from a finished headline onto other artistic text
unify outline weight and colour across a diagram
avoid: copying colour only: Color Eyedropper is simpler
documents built on styles: change the Object Style instead so every object updates together
copying size or position by accident: untick Transformations before clicking targets

review.changes: how: removed the unverified Shift-to-resample modifier. Script calls and the cdrCopyProperties names checked against the harvest; no other change.

cards.name: Color Eyedropper
cards.summary: Samples a colour from any object or bitmap on the page (or, with the desktop option, anywhere on screen) and then applies it: dropping it inside an object sets the fill, dropping it on the outline sets the outline colour. Only colour is copied, never other attributes.
cards.how: Pick it from the Eyedropper flyout. Set the sample size (single pixel or averaged area) and, if needed, Select from desktop in the property bar. Click to sample; the cursor becomes a paint bucket, then click inside a target object for its fill or on its outline for the outline colour. The property bar can also add the sampled colour to the document palette.
cards.script_api: Select the tool: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem "c109a053-50ab-4943-8edc-d374ec153e7e" or Application.ActiveTool = 119 (cdrToolEyeDropper). Do the job by script: Document.SampleColorAtPoint(x, y) or Document.SampleColorInArea(x1, y1, x2, y2, XSamples, YSamples) returns a Color, then Shape.Fill.ApplyUniformFill(Color) or Shape.Outline.Color.CopyAssign(Color). Sampling from the desktop outside CorelDRAW has no object-model call.
use_for: pull brand colours out of a placed photo or client logo bitmap
match a background panel to a colour in a product shot
build a palette from a reference image
recolour an outline to match a neighbouring fill
avoid: copying outline width, text style or effects: use Attributes Eyedropper
exact brand colours: type the CMYK / Pantone value instead, sampling an RGB bitmap gives an approximate colour
noisy or textured bitmaps with a 1-pixel sample: use an averaged sample size

review.changes: how: removed the unverified Shift-to-resample modifier. ActiveTool = 119 and the SampleColorAtPoint / SampleColorInArea signatures checked against the batch and harvest; no other change.

cards.name: Interactive Fill
cards.summary: Applies and edits an object's fill directly on the canvas: uniform, fountain (gradient), vector / bitmap / two-colour pattern, texture or PostScript fills, with on-object handles for gradient direction, centre and colour nodes and for pattern tile size, angle and skew.
cards.how: Select an object and press G. Dragging across the object creates a linear fountain fill from the drag start to the drag end; the property bar switches fill type (No fill, Uniform, Fountain, pattern types, Texture, PostScript) and fountain style (linear, elliptical, conical, rectangular). Drag the end handles to change direction and length, drag palette colours onto the fill vector to add colour nodes, double-click the vector line to add a node, and select a node to set its colour and transparency. For pattern fills the handles scale, rotate and skew the tile.
cards.script_api: Select the tool: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem "2c6e4e57-30d5-412a-bcc7-3c932dc7d7ad" or Application.ActiveTool = 71 (cdrToolFill). Apply the fill directly: Shape.Fill.ApplyFountainFill(StartColor, EndColor, Type, Angle, Steps, EdgePad, MidPoint, BlendType, CenterOffsetX, CenterOffsetY), then adjust Fill.Fountain (StartX ...) and its colour nodes; Fill.ApplyUniformFill, ApplyPatternFill, ApplyTextureFill, ApplyPostscriptFill for the other types.
use_for: gradient background for a poster or social card
metallic or glossy gradient on a logo shape
radial glow behind a product
pattern fill on packaging panels with tile size set by hand
fine-tuning gradient angle to follow a shape
avoid: soft, multi-directional shading on curved objects: use Mesh Fill
fading an object to transparent: use the Transparency tool, not fill nodes alone
many objects that need the same gradient: select them all and apply it once, or put it in an Object Style, rather than dragging on each

review.changes: avoid: "Edit Fill" removed from the shared-gradient tip (editing each fill does not share it); ApplyFountainFill argument order, ActiveTool = 71 and G checked against batch and harvest.

cards.name: Mesh Fill
cards.summary: Turns an object's fill into a grid of colour nodes: each node gets its own colour (and transparency) and colours blend smoothly between nodes, so you can paint photo-real shading such as fruit, skin, fabric folds or chrome. The mesh lines and handles bend to steer the colour flow.
cards.how: Select a single closed object and press M; a mesh grid appears. Set the number of rows and columns in the property bar, or double-click inside the mesh to add a node line. Select nodes (marquee-select several) and click a palette colour, or drop a colour onto a patch; drag nodes and their Bezier handles to move the colour. The property bar also sets node transparency and smooths the mesh colour. Medium confidence on the exact property bar layout.
cards.script_api: Only selection is scriptable: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem "8f3b40f1-ced9-4efa-9295-0d048c88db58". Application.ActiveTool = 118 also enters this tool's state, but 118 is outside the cdrTools enum and the harvest saw the toolbox highlight a different button (Freehand Pick, fb9a380a-4bbb-23bd-4e45-2eeed3e485b1), so prefer InvokeItem. No harvested object-model call creates or edits a mesh fill; scripts can only detect one (ActiveDocument.SelectionInfo.IsMeshFillSelected / IsMeshFillPresent, or Shape.Type = cdrMeshFillShape (20)).
use_for: realistic fruit, droplet or product illustration
soft skin and fabric shading in vector character art
chrome or glossy highlights that a linear or radial gradient cannot follow
organic coloured blobs and aurora-style backgrounds
avoid: simple linear or radial shading: Interactive Fill is lighter and easier to edit
files bound for older EPS or some print RIPs: mesh fills may be rasterised or approximated on export, check the output
groups or many objects at once: it works on one object at a time
automated pipelines: nothing in the object model can build a mesh fill

review.changes: script_api: the detection call is reached through Document.SelectionInfo (there is no SelectionInformation property), and Shape.Type = cdrMeshFillShape (20) spelled out; named the button the toolbox showed after ActiveTool = 118 (Freehand Pick).

cards.name: Smart Fill
cards.summary: Click inside any area enclosed by overlapping or touching objects and lines, and Smart Fill builds a new closed object exactly the shape of that region, placed on top and filled with the chosen fill and outline; the original objects are left untouched.
cards.how: Pick it from the Fill Tools flyout. In the property bar set Fill options (use default / specify a colour / no fill) and Outline options (use default / specify width and colour / no outline). Click inside each enclosed region you want filled; every click creates a separate new object. Works on regions formed by any mix of shapes and crossing lines, so line art drawn with open paths can be coloured. Medium confidence on the exact property bar wording.
cards.script_api: Select the tool: FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem "af052244-1121-4a82-b0d2-194106db742a" (no Application.ActiveTool value; the harvest read back -1). No harvested call is documented as filling the region at a point; rebuild a region with Shape.Intersect(TargetShape, LeaveSource, LeaveTarget) or Shape.Trim on closed shapes, then Fill.ApplyUniformFill. ShapeRange.CreateBoundary(x, y, PlaceOnTop, DeleteSource) also takes a point, but the harvest only describes it as "creates a boundary shape around the items in the ShapeRange"; test what it builds at (x, y) before using it in place of this tool.
use_for: colouring hand-drawn line art without redrawing closed shapes
making a fillable shape from the overlap of two circles (Venn diagram)
building logo pieces from the gaps between strokes
creating a cut or vinyl shape from an enclosed area of a layout
avoid: regions that are not fully closed: the click finds no area or picks a larger one; close the gap first
colour that must follow later edits of the line art: the new object does not update, redo it or use shaping commands
the outer silhouette of a whole group: use Object > Shaping > Boundary instead

review.changes: script_api: removed the unsupported claim that CreateBoundary makes only the outer outline (it takes an x, y point and the harvest does not say what that point does), now flagged as untested.
